title: Simulating Lead Routing and Customer Data Reuse in Industrial CRM–ERP Workflows
content: Nearly three quarters of the simulated time saving in industrial lead routing came from shorter waits for staff. At the supplier studied, leads entered a customer relationship management (CRM) system, while accepted quotations became orders in an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. Arena models traced each workflow from lead registration to order entry or closure. In SimPy, 400 paired replications per setting separated the effect of routing from those of staffing and contact policy. Across matched settings, redesigned routing shortened mean time per lead by 181.3 hours (simultaneous 95% confidence interval, 172.0–190.7 hours). A second representative shortened queues without changing order counts. A retry after an unanswered call yielded 6.7 additional orders per 100 leads. Of 1,561 selected sales orders from 252 quotations, 114 lacked a buyer. If related orders could share verified customer details, one entry per affected quotation would save 308 staff-hours at an assumed 4 hours per update. Completing those fields earlier shortened the path to ERP when late entry sent a prepared order back to sales.
